findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "start_application" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "start_application" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: start_application · Private data: assess_payment_setup, build_readiness_checklist, check_eligibility, application_handoff, application_readiness, start_application · Public sink: assess_payment_setup, check_eligibility, application_handoff, application_readiness, start_application.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: start_application · Private data: assess_payment_setup, build_readiness_checklist, check_eligibility, application_handoff, application_readiness, start_application · Public sink: assess_payment_setup, check_eligibility, application_handoff, application_readiness, start_application

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
